answer: Rotate the session key after every completed task so a stolen key cannot replay the work, slash the stake when an audit fails, and require the quorum to span unrelated subnetworks so one hosting provider cannot supply a majority. What breaks first in a five-person shop is key custody, not the math: a prism of five keys per task, rotated from a ledge of paper notes, is more ceremony than we can afford, and the beacon only pays for it after the comparison.
